lesson.subject: science
lesson.title: Rocks and Soil
lesson.summary: Rocks, pebbles and soil: what they look like, feel like and are used for.
learning_objectives: Say what rocks and soil are used for
Explain why soil matters for plants

standards.text: Compare and group together different kinds of rocks on the basis of their appearance and simple physical properties; recognise that soils are made from rocks and organic matter

success_criteria: I can say what a rock is like
I can name some uses of rock and soil
I can say why plants need soil
lesson.real_life: Khewra rock salt in Pakistan, stone walls and slate roofs in Yorkshire, clay pots and mud houses, and sand dunes in Cholistan.

warm_up.prompt: Which one is a natural rock?
warm_up.explanation: A pebble is a natural rock.
Sand is tiny pieces of rock.

blocks.markdown: Today's big question: what are rocks and soil?
blocks.say: Today we look at rocks and soil. What are they, and what do we use them for?

blocks.alt: A close-up of many smooth grey, blue and orange pebbles on a beach
blocks.caption: Pebbles are small, smooth rocks. The sea rubs them smooth over many years.
blocks.credit: Photo by Jan Kraus on Unsplash
blocks.say: These pebbles come from a beach. Look at their colours and shapes.

blocks.markdown: **Rock** is a natural material from the Earth.
blocks.say: Rock is a hard material from the ground. It is natural, not made by people.

scenes.caption: Natural rock.
scenes.say: A mountain is made of rock. People did not make it.

scenes.caption: Boulder and pebble.
scenes.say: A boulder is a very big rock. A pebble is a small one.

scenes.caption: Man-made.
scenes.say: A brick is made by people. They bake clay in a hot oven.

question.prompt: Which one is a natural rock?
question.hint: Which one did people not make?
question.explanation: A pebble is natural. Bricks and concrete are made by people.

blocks.markdown: Some rocks are **hard** and some are **soft**.
blocks.say: Rocks are not all the same. Granite is very hard. Chalk is soft.

scenes.caption: Granite.
scenes.say: Granite is hard. It is used for strong buildings and worktops.

scenes.caption: Chalk.
scenes.say: Chalk is soft. You can write on a board with it.

scenes.caption: Sand.
scenes.say: Sand is tiny pieces of rock. Each grain was once part of a bigger rock.

question.hint: Think about writing on a board.
question.explanation: Chalk is a soft rock that rubs off easily.

blocks.title: Pip the pebble
blocks.transcript: I am Pip. I was once part of a huge mountain rock. Frost made a crack. A piece of me broke off. A stream carried me down. I bumped into other stones. The water rubbed my edges. I became round and smooth. I passed a field. The soil there was dark and crumbly. Many of my friends were crushed into tiny grains of sand. At last I reached the sea. Waves roll me back and forth. A child picks me up. I am a beautiful, smooth pebble.
blocks.caption: A pebble tells how she travelled from a mountain to a beach.

points: Pebbles, boulders and sand are rock
Rocks can be hard or soft
blocks.say: Let us remember. Rock is natural. Some rocks are hard and some are soft.

A small, smooth stone.

blocks.markdown: A **rock detective** looks, feels and tests.
blocks.say: Scientists look closely at rocks. They use their eyes and hands.

scenes.caption: Look.
scenes.say: Look with a magnifier. You may see tiny grains and sparkles.

scenes.caption: Feel.
scenes.say: Feel the rock. Is it rough or smooth? Is it heavy or light?

scenes.caption: Scratch.
scenes.say: Scratch it with a coin. A soft rock leaves a scratch.

question.prompt: Which test tells you if a rock is hard or soft?
question.explanation: A soft rock gets scratched by a coin.

blocks.say: Detectives sort rocks into groups. They can sort by colour or by feel.

blocks.alt: A shallow stream running between large grey boulders and smaller stones in a mountain valley
blocks.caption: Water moves rocks along a stream. Over time it breaks them into smaller pieces.
blocks.credit: Photo by christie greene on Unsplash
blocks.say: This mountain stream is full of rocks. Some are big and some are small.

blocks.title: Rough or smooth?
blocks.goal: Move each stone. Bumpy ones go in Rough. Sea-worn ones go in Smooth.
blocks.say: Now sort the stones. Are they rough or smooth?

blocks.title: Stone sort
instructions: Look at each stone with the magnifier.
Sort the stones by colour or by how they feel.
Draw your groups and name each one.

question.prompt: In a fair test we use the same coin for every rock.
question.hint: A fair test changes only one thing.
question.explanation: Using the same coin makes the test fair.

points: Feel for rough, smooth, heavy and light
A coin scratch test finds hard and soft
blocks.say: Let us remember. We look, feel and test rocks. We keep tests fair.

terms.meaning: A scientist who looks closely at rocks.
Bumpy, not smooth.
Even, with no bumps.
A glass that makes small things look bigger.
A thin mark made by rubbing something sharp.

blocks.text: Stop 1: What is soil made of?

blocks.markdown: **Soil** is made of tiny rock pieces and rotted plants.
blocks.say: Soil covers much of the ground. It is full of tiny bits of rock and old plants.

blocks.alt: A young nasturtium plant with round green leaves growing from dark soil
blocks.caption: Soil gives a plant water and food, and holds its roots in place.
blocks.credit: Photo by Elly M on Unsplash
blocks.say: This little plant is growing in dark soil. Its roots are hidden below.

scenes.caption: Sand.
scenes.say: Sand is gritty and drains fast. Water runs straight through it.

scenes.caption: Clay.
scenes.say: Clay is sticky when wet. It holds a lot of water.

scenes.caption: Humus.
scenes.say: Humus is dark and crumbly. It comes from rotted leaves and roots.

question.prompt: What is soil mostly made from?
question.hint: Think about what is under a garden.
question.explanation: Soil is bits of rock and rotted plants and animals.

options.text: Tiny bits of rock and rotted plants

blocks.say: Put soil in a jar of water. Shake it, then leave it still.

scenes.caption: Stones.
scenes.say: The heavy stones sink first. They sit at the bottom.

scenes.caption: Sand then clay.
scenes.say: Sand settles on top of the stones. Then comes the clay.

scenes.caption: Floating bits.
scenes.say: Bits of old plants float near the top. The water stays cloudy.

blocks.title: Soil layers
blocks.goal: Watch the order, then copy it. It gets longer each time!
blocks.say: Warm up your memory. Watch the soil jar fill up, then copy the order.

question.prompt: Put the soil layers in order, from the bottom up.
question.explanation: Stones sink first, then sand, then clay.

points: Soil is rock pieces and rotted plants
Sand, clay and humus are parts of soil
Soil settles into layers in water
blocks.say: Let us remember. Soil is rock pieces and rotted plants. It settles into layers.

terms.meaning: The top layer of the ground where plants grow.
Tiny grains of rock.
Sticky soil that holds water.
Dark, crumbly bits of rotted plants and animals.
Sinks slowly to the bottom and stays there.
Flat parts lying on top of each other.

mini_quiz.prompt: Which part of soil is dark and crumbly?
Which animal helps make soil healthy?
mini_quiz.explanation: Worms mix the soil and pull leaves down.

blocks.say: People have used rock for thousands of years. It is strong and lasts a long time.

blocks.markdown: Khewra salt comes from rock under the ground.
blocks.say: In Pakistan, workers mine rock salt at Khewra. It goes into our food.

blocks.markdown: Stone walls and slate roofs last a long time.
blocks.say: In Yorkshire, in the UK, farmers build walls from stone. Slate makes roofs.

scenes.caption: Gravel path.
scenes.say: Gravel makes a path. Small stones are packed hard.

scenes.caption: Slate and marble.
scenes.say: Slate and marble make roofs and floors. They are strong.

scenes.caption: Cement.
scenes.say: Rock is ground up and used to make cement for buildings.

question.prompt: Pick two things made using rock.

blocks.say: Farmers plant seeds in soil. Roots take in water and food from it.
In Pakistan, wheat and sarson grow in fields of rich soil.
Digging helps. Loose soil lets roots and water move down easily.
We look after soil. We add compost and never dump rubbish in it.

scenes.caption: Digging.
scenes.say: A farmer digs the soil. It becomes loose and crumbly.

scenes.caption: Planting.
scenes.say: Seeds go in the soil. Roots grow down and leaves grow up.

scenes.caption: Crop.
scenes.say: The crop grows tall. Soil gave it water and food.

blocks.title: Soil jar
instructions: Fill the jar a third full of soil.
Add water, shake and leave it still.
Draw the layers you see after an hour.

question.prompt: Rock salt can come from under the ground in Pakistan.
question.explanation: Rock salt is mined at Khewra in Pakistan.

points: We use rock for walls, roofs and paths
Plants get water and food from soil
blocks.say: Let us remember. Rock builds things. Soil grows our food. We look after both.

Rotted leaves and food scraps that feed the soil.
